title: Rav Acha, brother of Mar Achai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in Shabbat 111b according to Hyman’s report of all the old printings and the reading known to Yuchasin. The text he calls “our reading” is: “Rav Achadvoi, brother of Mar Acha—or from Acha—asked.”

notes.text: דמן אחא means “from Acha,” not “of Mar Acha.” The exact relation of this alternative qualifier to the preceding brother designation remains unresolved.

The saved whole Davidson Shabbat111b paragraph explicitly has Rav Achadvoi, brother of Mar Acha. The saved whole Jerusalem1962 Epstein Kiddushin8 scalar reports the alternative דמן אחא and Rabbenu Chananel’s מדאחה as a place-name reading, in a secondary scholarly survey. It supports the rival qualifier from Acha, not an extra brother relation or a new inspection of those manuscripts/commentaries. Hyman owns the all-old-printings and Yuchasin claims; his phrase our reading is explicitly his edition’s wording.

In the consulted Vilna edition, Rabbeinu Chananel on Shabbat 111b takes the phrase as a place name. Maharshal’s Chokhmat Shlomo, catalogued at Shabbat 112a:1, gives the brother reading and records “from Acha” as an alternative, citing Tosafot Shantz in Rabbeinu Chananel’s name. Kiddushin 22b has a separate occurrence of Rav Achai [bar Adda] from Acha. The exact old printings and the passage in Yuchasin still need collation.
